validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed independent of GEM/wiki. This is a real, actively-discussed bilateral proposal, not a hallucination or GEM-only entity. Found continuous, dated, multi-source coverage spanning almost 2 years: (1) Sept 2024 — Nigeria's Min. of Petroleum (Gas) Ekperikpe Ekpo met Libya's Oil Minister Khalifa AbduAlsadik/Abdul-Sadig at Gastech Houston (africanenergycouncil.org 2024-09-23, byline Petlong Dakhling; pipeline-journal.net 2024-09-25, byline Daniel Onyango — same underlying event, different orgs/authors); (2) July 2025 — follow-up at OPEC Global Seminar, Vienna, between Abdul-Sadig and Nigeria's Min. of State for Petroleum (Oil) Heineken Lokpobiri (agcnewsnet.com 2025-07-13); (3) Sept 2025 — Gastech Milan meeting between Abdel Sadeg, Nigeria's Min. of State for Petroleum (Gas) Ekperekpe Ekpo, and NNPC CEO Bayo Ojulare, agreeing to exchange technical data ahead of an MoU (libyaherald.com 2025-09-11); (4) Sept 2025 — independent financial press (ecofinagency.com 2025-09-15) and paywalled energynews.pro (2025-09-16, datePublished verified via schema.org metadata) both report the Libya corridor is being studied at ~3,300 km, explicitly distinguished from the Nigeria-Algeria Trans-Saharan pipeline (~4,000 km) and the Nigeria-Morocco pipeline (5,560 km) — i.e. this is its own distinct project, not a relabeled NMGP segment, resolving an initial worry that the Sept 2024 stories (which cited a 5,600 km / 13-country West-Africa-then-Morocco route almost identical to NMGP's) meant this was really NMGP being double-counted. It appears the project's conception has evolved/been clarified since 2024: early reporting framed it as 'route NMGP through Libya instead of Algeria' (a 2022 Libyan proposal) using NMGP's figures, but 2025–26 reporting describes a shorter, more direct Nigeria→(Niger/Chad)→Libya→Mediterranean corridor. (5) March 2026 — libyareview.com describes a $20bn Nigeria-Chad-Libya-Sicily corridor with up to 30 bcm/y planned capacity, still 'proposed', investors being sought. (6) April 2026 (most recent, updated May 2026) — libyaherald.com reports Libya's Ministry of Oil and Gas 'Nigeria-Niger-Libya Gas Pipeline Project Committee' held a technical/coordination meeting reviewing preliminary engineering studies and MoU development — confirms the project is alive and in continuous, incremental progress, now with Niger formally named as a transit country. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both correctly recorded — every source describes an international gas-export trunk line, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the 6-pipeline Libya roster — the other 5 (Sirte Gulf, NC 41-Mellitah, E Structure-Mellitah, DP3–DP4–Sabratha x2) are all short domestic Libyan gas-field/plant tie-ins with construction status; none plausibly overlaps this transnational Nigeria-to-Libya proposal. No duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: StartCountryOrArea=Nigeria / EndCountryOrArea=Libya confirmed by every source (the project is literally named for this Nigeria→Libya axis in all of them). SPEC: ProposalYear=2024/ProposalMonth=9 confirmed — matches the Sept 2024 Gastech Houston meeting in both original sources. Length/Diameter/Capacity are blank in the sheet and I am leaving them blank: reported lengths conflict materially across sources and time (5,600 km in the original Sept 2024 stories vs. ~3,300 km in Sept 2025 reporting vs. a 30 bcm/y capacity and no length cited in the March 2026 libyareview piece) — this reflects genuine route evolution/uncertainty in a still-preliminary proposal, not a value I can confidently pin down.

fills.researcher_notes: Left blank rather than fabricate a single number: africanenergycouncil.org/pipeline-journal.net (Sept 2024) report 5,600 km, but that figure and 13-country route match the separate, longer-established Nigeria-Morocco Gas Pipeline (5,560 km) almost exactly — consistent with 2022-era Libyan proposals to reroute NMGP via Libya. Later independent reporting (ecofinagency.com and energynews.pro, both Sept 2025) instead describes a shorter, more direct ~3,300 km Nigeria–Libya corridor via the Mediterranean/Greenstream link, explicitly distinguished from NMGP's 5,560 km. libyareview.com (March 2026) gives no length at all. The project's own route appears to still be in flux (2026 renaming to 'Nigeria-Niger-Libya' suggests the alignment is still being finalized), so any single Length value would likely be wrong within months. Recommend leaving blank until an MoU/route is finalized.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=proposed is still correct and current as of the newest evidence I could find (April 2026, updated May 2026 per libyaherald.com), only 3 months before today. Progress has been continuous and incremental, not stalled: Sept 2024 ministerial meeting at Gastech Houston -> July 2025 follow-up at OPEC Vienna -> Sept 2025 Gastech Milan meeting agreeing to exchange technical data ahead of an MoU -> March 2026 reporting on a $20bn Nigeria-Chad-Libya-Sicily corridor (30 bcm/y target, investors being sought) -> April 2026 Libyan Ministry of Oil and Gas 'Nigeria-Niger-Libya Gas Pipeline Project Committee' technical/coordination meeting reviewing preliminary engineering studies and discussing the MoU. No FID, no construction start, no MoU signature yet reported anywhere, so 'proposed' remains the right bucket (not 'construction'). Given meetings roughly every 6-9 months and the most recent one just 3 months ago, this does not meet the 2-year proposed->shelved dormancy threshold — it's an active, if slow-moving, proposal. Note the project is now sometimes styled 'Nigeria-Niger-Libya Gas Pipeline' (Niger added as a named transit country) in 2026 reporting — worth a name/route watch at next update but not a basis for a status change now.

summary: P7102 Nigeria–Libya Gas Pipeline: existence strongly confirmed (multi-source, ~2 years of continuous ministerial-level activity through April 2026), correctly classified as a Gas transmission pipeline, no duplicate in the Libya roster, Status=proposed reconfirmed with April 2026 evidence; Length left unfilled due to a genuine, unresolved conflict between an early 5,600km/NMGP-like figure (2024) and a later ~3,300km distinct-corridor figure (2025-26).
